evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.240: cum esset cum eō dē amiculā rixātus (Lewis & Short s.v. rixor)
Hor. Ep. 1.18.15: dē lānā caprīnā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Rixor: to quarrel, wrangle (Lewis & Short: rare but classical).

evidence: Caes. BC 3.19: altercārī cum … incipit (Lewis & Short s.v. altercor)
Liv. 3.68: mulierum rītū inter nōs altercantēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Altercor is to dispute, have words with someone (cum aliquō, inter sē); lītigāre is to quarrel, dispute (quā dē rē lītigātis inter vōs?, Plaut. Rud. 4.4.16, Lewis & Short).
Argūmentor is to reason, to bring proofs (Lewis & Short), not to quarrel; for bickering say rixārī or jūrgāre.
